item.title: Designing an End-to-End Local Fund Audit Workflow: Tasks, Stages, and Process Flow
item.description:
Designing an End-to-End Local Fund Audit Workflow

An effective audit management system is built on a clearly defined workflow. Every audit activity should have a designated owner, a predecessor task, a successor task, and clearly identified decision points. This ensures accountability, transparency, and complete tracking of audit observations from initiation to final settlement.

This article presents a structured Local Fund Audit workflow suitable for implementation in an Audit Management System or an AuditOnline platform.

item.title: Local Fund Audit and Internal Audit in Sikkim: A Complete Beginner's Guide for Accounts Officers
item.description:
Local Fund Audit and Internal Audit in Sikkim

A Complete Beginner’s Guide for Newly Appointed Accounts Officers

“Every rupee of public money belongs to the people. Audit ensures that every rupee is accounted for.”

Introduction

Financial accountability is one of the cornerstones of good governance. Every government department, municipality, panchayat, autonomous body, and public institution receives public funds to implement schemes and deliver services. Citizens expect these funds to be spent legally, efficiently, economically, and for the intended purpose.

item.title: GST Audit Explained: A Complete Beginner-to-Expert Guide to Internal and Departmental GST Audit
item.description:
GST Audit Explained: A Complete Beginner-to-Expert Guide

Goods and Services Tax (GST) follows a self-assessment system, where every registered taxpayer is responsible for determining the correct tax liability, paying taxes on time, and filing accurate returns. Since the tax authorities do not verify every transaction before accepting returns, audits play a crucial role in ensuring compliance.

This guide explains the GST audit process from the basics to advanced concepts, covering internal audits, departmental audits, audit procedures, notices, observations, replies, and practical audit checklists.

item.title: Comprehensive Guide to RTI Proactive Disclosure and Internal Audit Functions in Sikkim
item.description:
Comprehensive Guide to RTI Proactive Disclosure and Internal Audit Functions in Sikkim

Transparency and accountability are the bedrock of effective financial management in government. Under Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, public authorities are mandated to proactively disclose key information regarding their organization, functions, duties, and operational procedures. This proactive disclosure minimizes the necessity for individual citizens to file formal requests while fostering public trust.

This article details the institutional framework, RTI proactive disclosures, and core objectives of both the Sikkim Local Fund Audit (SLFA) and the Internal Audit (IA) Division under the Finance Department, Government of Sikkim.

item.title: Strengthening Public Financial Management: A Comprehensive Guide to Internal Audit Guidelines and the 3 E's
item.description:
Introduction

In the realm of public governance, ensuring financial accountability, transparency, and optimal utilization of public resources is paramount. Governments handle vast amounts of public funds, execute complex programs, and manage extensive assets. To maintain fiscal discipline and prevent irregularities, organizations rely heavily on robust oversight mechanisms. Among these, the Internal Audit Organisation acts as a crucial catalyst from within, safeguarding public funds and streamlining department functions.

This blog explores the comprehensive framework governing internal audits—drawing from foundational guidelines (such as the 1992 and 2005 supplementary regulations)—while diving deep into core concepts like internal control mechanisms and the classic performance framework known as the 3 E’s (Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness).
